messages:
amanda: Heads-up — signalboard just flagged a persistent divergence between reported token spend and cached-savings for model-redwood-v2. Not huge yet but trending.

dinesh: got the alert. can you paste a screenshot or the query? curious if it's a sampling artifact.

amanda: quick screenshot in thread. metric looks like ~12% higher token exposure vs dashboard estimate for last 3 hours. attaching raw query we used:

```sql
SELECT model, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(cache_saved_tokens) as cached
FROM invocation_metrics
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '3 hours'
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY tokens desc
LIMIT 10;
```

sara: thanks. two immediate suspects: 1) cache fingerprinting mismatch after the rollout last night, 2) our sampling rate for big requests (we downsample long seqs).

joel: UI question — if we expose this on the signalboard, should we show absolute token delta or normalized per-invocation? On-call needs quick triage.

amanda: prefer absolute + % change. absolute tells cost impact, % highlights regressions. maybe tooltip with per-invocation median.

maya: agree. also think we need an annotations layer for rollout tags (canary window) so SREs see if a deploy correlates.

cost-alert-bot: Alert created: COST_DRIFT model-redwood-v2 (severity: low) — 3h drift +12%. Link: https://console/internal/signalboard/alerts/2351234567

joel: for the backend event, do we compute the drift from sampled data or from aggregated billing ledger? different guarantees.

dinesh: currently signalboard uses aggregated sampler (1/10 on >2k-token invocations) to reduce cardinality. billing ledger is eventual and slower.

sara: could we run a differential check: recompute for the top 50 offending invocations with full fidelity to confirm? cheap and targeted.

amanda: ok i'll kick off a job for the top 100 by tokens and compare. if they match, it's on attribution logic, otherwise sampling bias.

joel: UX follow-up: add a "recompute on demand" button in the panel that runs the full-fidelity check for the selected window. shows progress and diff.

maya: +1. make it gated by role to avoid accidental runs. also surface estimated cost of recompute (e.g., "reads ~120k rows").

dinesh: technical note — attribution currently assigns cache savings to the inferred route via first-party headers. sticky routing changes last week can cause misattribution across tenant fallthroughs.

sara: oh interesting — so a request routed to fallback model would still carry cache credits to the original route in some cases?

dinesh: yes, if KV fingerprint preserved but route tag not updated when fallback occurs. need to thread route-tag through the runtime on fallback path.

amanda: that's actionable. if we fix route-tagging, signalboard should immediately converge.

joel: API debate: should the panel expose a new endpoint that returns the raw exposure rows for a window (privacy-filtered) or only pre-aggregated deltas? ops wants rows for fast triage.

maya: prefer pre-aggregated by default, and an opt-in rows endpoint for trusted roles. rows endpoint should redact user prompt content and only include hashed request ids.

sara: agree. add sampling metadata fields to all responses: sample_rate, sample_bias_score, recompute_status.

amanda: job done — launched targeted recompute for top-100. results ETA ~2m.

cost-alert-bot: Job 8812 started: full_fidelity_recompute (top_100) — will post results.

amanda: recompute finished. outcome: sample bias explains ~9% of the drift; remaining ~3% is due to route-tagging bug. attaching small diff.

```diff
- cached_savings_reported: 234,512
+ cached_savings_actual: 256,123
- token_exposure_reported: 1,982,345
+ token_exposure_actual: 1,982,345
```

dinesh: nice catch. i'll open a PR to thread route tags on fallback in the runtime. quick estimate: ~3 developer hours + rollout.

joel: on the panel UX, let's add a compact header: "estimated annualized drift" extrapolated if current rate persists, and a small help icon linking to attribution docs.

maya: also add an "impact to billing" calc for finance view (monthly projection). ensure it's clear assumptions and confidence.

sara: and emit a telemetry event when someone clicks "recompute" so we can see how often ops uses it and whether it stabilizes metrics.

amanda: will draft a short PR checklist for the panel changes: recompute button, rollout tag annotation, sample metadata fields, telemetry event. looping in @dinesh for runtime fix.

dinesh: thanks. ping me on the PR. i'll also add an automated smoke check in the canary that validates route-tag parity on fallback.

joel: sweet. good example of signal -> quick triage -> fix. can we capture this as a short postmortem-like note in #eng-platform after it's merged? helps docs.

amanda: yes will drop a 3-line summary after merge. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks team. feel better having a recompute guardrail in the UX.

cost-alert-bot: Alert resolved: COST_DRIFT model-redwood-v2 — root cause: routing tag mismatch (fixed by PR #4127)."
